LESSON: DRAWING AND PAINTING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.2: Drawing and Painting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Drawing and Painting, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to clean the brush after painting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Drawing and Painting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner watch videos to recognise how to mix colour by spraying and blowing

technique,

• Creativity and imagination: The learner explores colours mixing techniques in painting.

Values:
• Unity: The learner respects others’ opinions while talking about their own and peers' pictures.

• Social justice: The learner shares resources and responsibilities equitably while mixing coloured water paints.

6

Health promotion issues: The learner cleans the working area and washes hands after spraying paint.

Link to other learning areas:

Hygiene Activities: The learner takes care of hygiene by cleaning their hands after painting.
